lines: Eurovision Song Contest Asia The Philippines, with the song "Sobra-Sobra" by Carmelle, wins the inaugural Eurovision Song Contest Asia held in Bangkok, Thailand. (AFP) (AP)

2026 Bangladesh garment workers protests The Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association threatens to indefinitely close unrest-affected factories without pay under the Bangladesh Labour Act 2006, after ongoing wage protests force the shutdown of 55 units and halt production at 147 others. (The Business Standard)

Canada–Philippines relations, Free trade agreements of Canada Canadian prime minister Mark Carney announces that negotiations for a free-trade agreement (FTA) with the Philippines have concluded, with signing expected in 2027. The FTA would eliminate more than 90% of tariff lines. (AFP)
The Slagdijkstermolen windmill in Friesland, Netherlands, burns down. (Omrop Fryslân in Dutch)
Eight more people in Bangladesh are reported to have died from dengue fever, bringing this year's outbreak's death toll past 491. (BSS)

Crime in Bangladesh Border Guard Bangladesh seize 48 explosive gel sticks, 100 detonators, and 11 fuses during an operation along the Bangladesh–India border in Kanaighat Upazila, Sylhet District, Bangladesh. (BSS)
2026 European unrest 2026 French civil unrest Student protesters, unions, and the yellow vests hold another nationwide protest in France, with over 100,000 participants. (France 24) (Türkiye)

2027 South Sudanese general election The South Sudanese election commission postpones the country's first presidential and parliamentary elections since independence in 2011 from December 22, 2026, to February 11, 2027, amid political tensions and continuing violence. (AFP via RFI)

The Italian Data Protection Authority [it] fines American technology company Meta for €805 million (US$887 million) after it was found that the Facebook Android app had access to users' photos and videos without specific consent or disclosure. (BBC News) (Reuters)
